## Priority order and completion gates

### P1 — Local WASM original-game acceptance, then Workers deployment

Get the actual original KOTOR game to a working main menu and playable state inside the existing local prototype at `http://127.0.0.1:47653/`. Preserve the same page and existing prototype, use GL4ES to translate required rendering behavior rather than removing calls, and finish the guest ABI, GL translation, startup/lifecycle and build-reuse work. Measure cold/warm/restart startup, remove the dominant measured bottlenecks, and avoid rebuilding unchanged artifacts. Finish lazy game-file access from incremental file/chitin.key drops or the whole-folder picker, plus supported optional GOG/Steam ownership connection; read needed files on demand rather than requiring an upload of the whole install. Accept `chitin.key` as the user's stated ownership/installation proof for this local workflow, while distinguishing that from store-authenticated entitlement; do not publish private game files or keys in the Worker. Determine and provision actual runtime dependencies so launch does not expose failed Wine/Mono installer dialogs. Support local `.holo` save/load and relevant authoring parity. Accept the local result through real launch, rendered menu, live controls/input, persistence and reload, with diagnostics for any failure. **Only after that local gate passes**, publish with Wrangler to the authorized `https://kptas-demo.bocloud.workers.dev/` URL and verify the live result.

**Gate:** original game reaches main menu and continues into playable gameplay on the existing localhost page; no setup/installer error dialog blocks launch; runtime input, rendering and required persistence work; no fake screenshot or source-only receipt stands in for interaction. Then deployment and live verification. The user has authorized the later deployment but explicitly required the local main-menu gate first.

### P2 — Complete the native GOG K1 TAS, not a single-mechanic demo

Implement and qualify the whole native TAS from the original Discord request: independently packaged/lightweight `KPTASInterface` / `InputInterfaceTelos` in KPHarness, with KotorPhasor optional; holorecords retaining each supported state boundary across memory, threads, clocks, files, graphics state/resources and handles, plus inputs, ancestry and provenance; genuine restore to the selected frame/tick; and separately configurable TOML checkpoint/replay, which must never be presented as restore. Default precision is frame-level. Make the virtual clock rate configurable only within rates proven compatible with the measured game-loop/input boundaries; do not assume rates must be multiples of 30 without evidence. The user's portable reference-math default is already represented in source configuration, but qualify whether the actual K1 callsites use it and whether it preserves game behavior on the declared profiles. Keep faithful keyboard, mouse motion and buttons through variable-duration loads, saves, Alt+F4 and relaunch. Preserve base-game behavior, glitches and RNG. Provide general pause, step, rewind, fast-forward, seek, save/load, input editing, branching and retry; unify command and visual control over one session/controller; show the actually applied input and real position; persist acknowledged work and drafts across failures and binary changes; and finish the compact, reactive, customizable/persistent in-game workspace, hotkeys and useful debugger widgets. Measure end-to-end authoring throughput. Queue native changes into coherent reviewed builds and qualify on the actual native GOG K1 game. Do not spend this priority on particular mechanics; route demonstrations follow.

**Gate:** native GOG K1 launches with the accepted pin and independently installable TAS; one controllable TAS surface drives the game; holorecord state/input/provenance survives save/load/relaunch; genuine rewind and step restore and continue without crashing or corrupting state; checkpoint/replay remains explicitly separate; the clock-rate constraints are derived from observed engine boundaries; reference math is the configured default and its actual game callsites/results are qualified without claiming universal determinism; gameplay/RNG and supported inputs remain faithful and repeatable in the declared environment; UI, actual input display, playback pacing, authoring actions, crash recovery, and a useful measured throughput all work. These requirements map to `standalone-release`, `crash-durable-work`, `full-memory-restore`, `frame-clock-boundaries`, `graphics-audio-restoration`, `single-controller-authoring`, `tas-debugger-interface`, `ui-customization-acceptance` and the 50 individually listed UI objectives. The historical proposal for actors, positions, equipment, stats and animation is a lower-level specification of what holorecord restoration must preserve; it is not satisfied by video or input-only score files.

### P3 — Make speedrun inputs usable

Continue acquiring the largest practical set of relevant K1/K2 submissions, prioritizing R4NG3 as requested and other runs with useful visible keyboard/mouse or actual input files. Align observations against source video timestamps and game events, extract keyboard, mouse motion/buttons and durations, preserve provenance and uncertainty, resolve bindings, assemble interchangeable/mergeable sections, and import only honest, inspectable score/binding artifacts. Qualify actual playback in the TAS and repair divergences at the relevant game state when RNG/state differs; never invent unreadable inputs or label observations as executable input. The submitted-run corpus is a means to repeatable tool playback, not merely a report. Current disabled projections include: Otterito m3jj03qz HLS segment 41, 204 presentations with non-redundant `rmb`, `1`, `numenter`, `a`, `s`, and `w` transitions, PTS 42602850–42907410 at 1/90000 and 16/17 ms intervals (projection SHA-256 `0a7dbf29115b7b252df14209e3794dab4e8056f08c9cb7b2e73c69e64b8d064a`; sidecar SHA-256 `558865778120dda53a8680287c686b4035741995605bed1f3c9eb79169677f2f`); R4NG3 y4ol3jkz Sith Base menu transition, 63 presentations with Esc/menu, Down/Enter and “Save the current game” prompt, PTS 3132416–3148288 at 1/15360 and 256 ticks per presentation (projection SHA-256 `cf7eac15d0d837dc994e2daa6e1ca43319e1f346b173290694714c5b28ddfb88`; sidecar SHA-256 `d1ba430bb1999871a91441bc818ea782e4648460de83391ed42f675150b8072d`); and Otterito megnd53y part 7, 141 presentations/source frames 26789–26929 (assembled ordinals 288926–289066), 24 visible keyboard-state runs across A/D/S/Space/W, PTS 670183380–670393350 at 1/90000 with 16/17 ms intervals (projection SHA-256 `948ed25423e2ebcd1cb35b2dff77ad432c928245be4f3e22293b819053ecd637`; sidecar SHA-256 `7850fd536d212d6fbf947ad8e92b99eb7ad8f091d9d9f668c66a2679fe02e8fb`). The first Otterito span has 16 unresolved global lanes inactive and omits pointer motion; the second has all visible keyboard lanes classified, while mouse crops vary and pointer motion remains omitted; the R4NG3 mouse crop is stable. None establish physical holds, input polling/game-frame alignment, or replayability, so all remain disabled and not replay-qualified.

### P4 — Finish continuous full-run execution and requested clips

Provide a continuous agent-authored run serialized through TAS inputs without screenshot-by-screenshot conversational operation. Complete The Routine with frame precision in under one minute, using the relevant speedrun save, including the deliberate missed input, pause, obvious rewind, correction, continuation and final playable reload; capture the actual game and TAS controls continuously at the claimed rate, without splices, retiming or substituted frames. Show seek/step/fast-forward behavior where requested, preserve real-time claims, and separately label any accelerated derivative. Also complete the requested short/succinct demo clips. The Routine clip is evidence of the system, not a replacement for the native TAS product.

### P5 — Requested mechanics and route showcases

After the native controller is useful, perform Endar Spire DLZ entirely through the TAS and show genuine pause/rewind; investigate AMG and other requested mechanics; produce repeatable swoop runs and the no-warp Taris apartment chain; then build the full K1 Any% Unrestricted run. Use qualified reference runs and saves and preserve failures/provenance.

### P6 — Remaining support, release, reverse-engineering and operations

Implement and qualify semantic RPG mode on a no-GPU/no-device host without fake devices, K2 Windows/Linux support, all `m5-current-review.md` issues, user-voice documentation, truthful branding/demo/download/donation path, AgentDecompile cross-matching of absolute references across the K1/K2 source and corpus binaries, and `.gpr`/shared-project physical-binary extraction that updates `corpus-work`. Follow AgentDecompile usage guidance and preserve its existing service on port8080; avoid needless fresh-JVM startup for each request. Complete the requested TAS-only integration diagrams, storage reserves and recurring bottleneck/plan/accountability process. Maintain 50 GB free on NVMe and 500 GB on MyBook using justified stale/duplicate cleanup while protecting active work, unique data and raw evidence. Preserve the deferred website scope; archive superseded guidance only after its unique content is reconciled and a recoverable copy verified. Do not claim unsupported platforms or community eligibility.

### P7 — Telos Core, separately installable modules, and later Telos Exchange work

Complete this ecosystem at P7, preserving independent package delivery and the P1/P2 runtime acceptance lanes. Telos Core owns the supported runtime, debugger, package lifecycle and installation root; TAS, Lua and other additions remain separately versioned packages installed into Core. Core must remain useful without TAS or Lua. New additions use stable, managed high-level APIs; privileged native adapters are separately declared and target-qualified. Browser/native TAS/debugger parity and the game-agnostic debugger capability layer are parallel objectives and proceed separately without consuming active P1/P2 runtime sessions. The current browser host/manifest is only an initial package boundary; native parity and independent package delivery remain open. Keep the broad Exchange catalog, compatibility/trust discovery, collections, publishing/discussion and community maintenance as later P7 work, integrated into the actual Kolto Labs site rather than a standalone site. KPM remains excluded from the supported launch path and must not be touched when refusal is applied.

## Execution method

- Maintain one native-game/build owner. Workers may prepare disjoint, reviewed slices; do not disturb the live game or replace its pinned artifacts. Batch compatible DLL changes, freeze and review the aggregate, build once, then obtain fresh game evidence.
- Use no more than three workers alongside the root in the current session. A queued owner is not a running worker. Keep independent WASM, native TAS, video-input and interface ownership explicit; adapt staffing to the P1/P2 gates.
- Model routing: use GPT-6 Astra for any subagent assigned to build, create, or modify GUI/interface elements; use GPT-6 Luna for other subagent assignments. Source-only audits and architecture inventories do not count as GUI implementation.
- Freeze and review all compatible runtime changes before production rebuilds. For WASM, coalesce the accepted GL4ES/ABI/timer/lifecycle changes and rebuild only the resulting shared source state; for native, batch compatible DLL changes behind one rig/build owner. Never make another worker's changes disappear or install a binary over an active owner.
- At every recurring review, inspect implementation/behavior and receipts—not typing, status reports, test counts, or files merely existing. Find the largest actual bottleneck, remove it, and update this plan’s state/next gate from evidence. Keep routine progress reporting and ETA bounded by measured operations; do not promise a finish time without evidence.
- Keep all game assets private/user-owned. Workers.dev contains only code and authorized hosting artifacts after local acceptance.

Five measured workflow bottlenecks and their shortest fixes:

1. Guest startup has not crossed its first render. Use the trace-enabled existing candidate to attribute the stalled process/thread and GL boundary; do not repeat pause/step screenshots or change GL/Wine speculatively.
2. Candidate admission was duplicated between its manifest and a hard-coded browser allowlist. Verify manifest hashes/sizes before selection and keep one admission receipt as the source of truth; this incident cost a full launch before surfacing.
3. Runtime compile/stage cycles are expensive and were started before one falsifiable hypothesis was frozen. Source receipts show an example compile+stage takes roughly three minutes. Batch all C/C++/Emscripten changes into one frozen snapshot, require a predicted trace/render delta, compile once, stage once, then launch once. Browser JS/HTML/CSS/descriptor edits do not need that compile; CSS and lifecycle-approved presentation updates can use opt-in HMR, while `original-game.js` edits need only a page reload.
4. Repeated cold launches and noisy storage/process load multiply latency. Keep the prior live tab intact, use one candidate session and one isolated writable profile, reuse the hash-verified root, and run one sequential hash read. The current root is NVMe-backed; removable-disk I/O is not this candidate's blocker.
5. Evidence/tool drift caused duplicate probes: the old Playwright attach path was already unavailable, the plan was stale about trace artifacts, and routine screenshots obscured the decisive state. Use CUA (already working), report only deltas from a single bounded receipt (session/release/root/profile, last guest log lines, thread states, presents), and update this plan at each gate. Do not repeat an unchanged probe; reroute after one bounded attempt without progress.

Acceleration protocol: static admission first (root digest/size, release asset manifest, launch URL parameters); then one live trace window of 60–90 seconds; then exactly one source-level fix group against the trace; only compile if the fix touches WASM/native objects or Emscripten link/worker settings; stage once; launch in the preserved tab; accept only a visible KOTOR menu/game with nonzero present and an input-driven UI change. This avoids rebuilds for page-level issues and makes every build answer one measurable question. No tests, deployment, or completion claim.

Implemented `telos_vm_copy_paused_registers(pid,output,capacity)`, independently of optional dispatch tracing. It holds the control mutex and requires a nonempty full all-worker pause barrier, no run-until-present/step owner/permit, a real PID and complete CPUs. It returns up to 128 selected-PID rows, each 12 U32 words: tid,pid,state,saved EIP,eax,ecx,edx,ebx,esp,ebp,esi,edi. Unknown processes, bad bounds, missing CPUs and overflow refuse the capture with UINT_MAX; partial buffers never become successful captures. No host pointer, flags/FPU/SIMD, register write, CPU step or snapshot/restore operation is added. Existing parked-thread lifetime and kernel-wait departure synchronization is used; these are saved guest CPU values, not a wait-cause diagnosis or guaranteed next opcode.

The origin/session/request-checked bridge optionally advertises this actual export and routes a bounded `registers` capture under the pause barrier. It validates IDs/states/count, copies the current HEAP into named hex values before freeing, checks duplicate IDs and preserves architecture/semantics. The owner validates the exact x86 nine-register shape. New `createGuestRegisterAdapter()` routes `registers.read` with exactly `{pid}` through that owner, checks session and PID and exposes no second controller. The shell registers the adapter; source capability reports enable registers only when the actual runtime flag is true and guest memory is ready. Old runtimes retain unsupported registers. Registers UI uses the request service, requires a paused selected process, rejects stale session/PID results, displays Thread/Register/Saved value and keeps the explicit snapshot/next-instruction limitation. Its declared generic captured-register response permits at most 128 threads, 32 named registers/thread and 128-bit hexadecimal values; that shape supplies no arbitrary-game backend. Native/uploaded-game handlers still need real owner-qualified operations and their own actual values.

P1 source-only inspection confirmed x11_WarpPointer previously used only ARG8/ARG9 as absolute desktop coordinates. Parallel source inspection found shared watches/scans always interpreted little endian while generic target contracts already permit pointerBits/byteOrder. KOTOR now has getRuntimeTarget(), declaring the existing recognized-profile x86/PE32/windows-32 layout, pointerBits:32 and byteOrder:little. publishRuntimeSession and the app host's current-session getStatus use that same getter. Strings adds explicit UTF-16BE ASCII alongside ASCII/UTF-16LE, retaining both byte alignments, bounded tables and existing raw capture.
